Any other word - a synonym of best / only ('alone', 'just', 'the one', 'the rest', 'other', 'exception', 'took gold', 'star'), an order or table word, a streak word ('kept', 'continued', 'extended', 'another', 'deepened'), an equality word ('same', 'matched', 'equaled'), an intensity verb ('surged', 'tanked', 'sold off', 'in the green', 'higher', 'lower'), a number word ('three'), a month ('in October'), 'every' / 'all' / 'each', an arrow / medal emoji, or > < = - makes the sentence need to be a claim phrase verbatim. Numbers and moves are tied to their subject: each number goes right after the company / sector it belongs to ('$MSFT −1.13%', never '$MSFT +2.03%' when +2.03% is $AAPL's), and rose / fell / up / down must match the move of every company / sector it is said of (never a move the item does not give, never negated, never with will / could / may).
rules.claims: superseded by claim_phrases (kept for the direction / date reading): comparatives and superlatives (led, biggest, largest, worst, best, most, least, only, first, top, #1, record, 'outperformed every other') only as the item's claims state them: name only that claim's companies / sectors in that sentence; each claim has a polarity (best = top gainer, worst = top loser, null = no side) and a rank (1 = its one subject is #1; group = its subjects are the top N in order) and a metric (usd_change, pct_change, market_cap, ...): say the side with the noun ('top loser', 'led the drop', 'biggest gainer';
